answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may place jobs or vote on reputation. Accounts that collude to certify one another risk losing that stake when a completed task is challenged and independently verified. A lagoon of cheap wallets therefore cannot create influence for free: the attacker must buy and lock capital per identity, keep it tied up, and accept losses if the beacon of review exposes fabricated work. A crystal-clear rule is that deposits raise the cost of Sybils; they do not prove that identities are unique.
